Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

sample noun

a small part that shows what the whole is like

also samples, free sample, a taste, try a sample, specimen, foretaste

classical

Auct. Her. 4.6.9: purpurae, trīticī (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. sample (of product), after Vives

exemplum, exemplī n.

noun, second declension

a sample (of goods)

Its first sense, from eximere, to take out: what is taken out to show the rest (Lewis & Short). Its common senses are a copy, a pattern, a model to follow, an instance, and a warning to others (exemplum statuere in aliquem).

Other words

  • gustus, gustūs m. — a taste, a sample (of food, or of a writer’s work)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 4.27.5: Ad hunc gustum tōtum librum repromittō; Sen. Ep. 114.18: Gustum tibi dare voluī; Traupman 390: (foretaste, sample)

    A tasting, a taste; post-Augustan, not in Cicero (Lewis & Short). It is also the light first course of a Roman dinner, and taste as a sense (see taste).

Examples

  • Vidēs quam ācūta omnia quam apta quam expressa. Ad hunc gustum tōtum librum repromittō

    You see how sharp it all is, how neat, how vivid. On the strength of this sample I promise you the whole book is the samePlin. Ep. 4.27.5

  • Gustum tibi dare voluī: tōtus hīs contexitur liber.

    I wanted to give you a sample: the whole book is woven out of things like these.Sen. Ep. 114.18

See also taste, blood test, goods, shop.
